appliesTo: Every production-art brief and every portrait/landscape CG family in the narrative-game profile.
failurePolicy: A brief or batch is not production-ready when wardrobe identity, scene context, continuity type, or shared-scene silhouette contrast is missing.

nika.silhouette: relaxed elegant Mediterranean tailoring with soft natural fabrics; practical movement and a readable feminine line
nika.formality: understated professional, adapting to travel, service spaces, office work and evening pressure
nika.forbiddenDefault: The same light shirt plus the same light trousers in every scene without an authored continuity reason.

matteo.role: composed, affluent, controlled, masculine Mediterranean elegance
matteo.silhouette: structured overshirt, jacket or tailored separates; mature shoulders and controlled vertical line
matteo.formality: confident adult host and owner, more structured than Nika and never her light-linen duplicate
matteo.forbiddenDefault: A pale linen uniform that duplicates Nika's colour, texture and relaxed silhouette.

elio.role: warm, approachable, sunlit, tactile kitchen professional
elio.silhouette: lighter, active workwear with rolled sleeves and clear kitchen/service function
elio.formality: approachable working staff; practical rather than managerial
signatureElements: white kitchen apron/uniform in kitchen scenes
upright kitchen knife with cookware context
dark work apron outside the kitchen when authored

leo.role: quiet, introspective, slightly artistic and architectural
leo.silhouette: slender architectural field layers, long vertical lines and a thoughtful working silhouette
leo.formality: professional but solitary; distinct from Matteo's host/owner structure
signatureElements: architectural field jacket or quiet coat

giulia.silhouette: practical housekeeping apron and rolled, serviceable layers
giulia.formality: experienced staff uniform with domestic warmth

bianca.silhouette: distinct supporting silhouette; never inherit Nika or Matteo's base look
signatureElements: one stable accessory declared by the brief

sceneRules: Wardrobe changes or visibly varies with time of day, location, temperature/atmosphere, formality, action and emotional tone.
Adjacent scenes without a time break may reuse an outfit; a location, time, social-context or long-duration change requires a new outfit or an explicit visual variation.
Every asset family declares outfit, accessories/props and continuity type for every involved character.
Shared-scene characters must have contrast in colour, cut, texture and costume role; faces alone are insufficient.
Portrait and landscape versions share identity and wardrobe facts but are independently composed and safe for their respective interface areas.
Character references remain authoritative for face, age, hair and body identity; wardrobe rework must not create a new character design.

dualFormat.invariant: Do not change wardrobe, identity, props or emotional beat between formats; change only intentional composition and framing.

requirements: Physical source PNG and runtime screenshot for both portrait and landscape, checked at exact Git HEAD and image SHA-256
Actual independent reviewer observations for each required character against attached canonical reference: face, age, hair and wardrobe
Match clothing and props between portrait/landscape; independent composition is allowed
Compare adjacent scenes when the narrative has no wardrobe-changing break; a time or social-context change requires an authored explanation
Evaluate unjustified repeated outfits across an episode; a consistent work uniform or continuous same-day action may be intentionally reused
No independent Web High pixel receipt or missing observations means NOT_VERIFIED; mechanical PASS is never artistic PASS
Do not regenerate images for minor P2/P3 wardrobe preferences or invent a PASS from an authored brief
